watcher_vs_disconnect_race.risk: Double-mutation / desync between the new watcher and onConfirmDisconnect.
reasoning: botStore.disconnect (bot.ts:65-68) sets current.value = null on success. The watcher then fires and sets showDisconnectModal.value = false. onConfirmDisconnect (bot.vue:86) also sets showDisconnectModal.value = false explicitly. Both writes assign the same value (false) to a boolean ref — Vue's ref setter is idempotent on === equality, so there is no extra reactivity flush, no double unmount, no observable race.
Error path: disconnect() throws BEFORE current is cleared. The watcher does NOT fire. onConfirmDisconnect's catch block (bot.vue:88-89) closes the modal explicitly. State is consistent.

closeDisconnectModal() (bot.vue:75-78) guards on disconnecting.value === true to prevent the user from cancelling mid-flight. The watcher intentionally does NOT respect that guard — on success it fires after the await resolves, so closing the modal one tick before the `finally` block clears `disconnecting` is the expected outcome. The DialogContent unmounts; no body-render artifact escapes.

No path observed where the watcher could reopen the modal or leave it in an inconsistent state. botStore.current can only transition null → Bot via successful fetch/connect; in both cases the modal is not yet open.

password_input_autofill_interaction.risk: Browser password managers store the bot token in their credential vault.
reasoning: Chrome (since 2014) and Firefox (since v30) deliberately ignore `autocomplete="off"` on `type="password"` fields so password managers continue to function. WHATWG-compliant, intentional vendor behaviour.

Practical consequence: when the user submits the connect form successfully, Chrome/Edge MAY offer to save the bot token as a password keyed to the settings URL. If accepted, the secret syncs across the user's signed-in devices via Google Password Manager (or Apple Keychain in Safari's case).
This is a NEW exposure surface that did not exist with `type="text"` + `autocomplete="off"` (text fields with `autocomplete="off"` are honoured by all major browsers).

Severity: minor. AC17 says the token must never leave the FRONTEND application code; a browser-controlled password vault is not application code. The token does not traverse the network beyond the legitimate /bot/connect POST. However, persisting the credential in the user's browser sync graph is exactly the kind of secondary exposure secrets-handling policies typically want to avoid.

Mitigation: switch to `autocomplete="new-password"`. Chrome/Edge interpret this as 'do not offer to save'. Firefox treats it as a hint not to autofill. The masking behaviour of `type="password"` is preserved; the shoulder-surf fix from round-1-finding-1 is unaffected.

Alternative (heavier): keep `type="password"` for masking, add an explicit `name=""` and `data-1p-ignore` / `data-lpignore="true"` to opt out of the major third-party managers (1Password, LastPass). This is overkill for a minor finding.

findings.title: Browser password manager may persist the bot token after successful connect
findings.description: After round-1 fix #1, the token input is `<input type="password" autocomplete="off" ...>` (bot.vue:125-135). On a successful submission, Chrome/Edge/Firefox MAY offer to save the field's last value as a password for the settings page origin. `autocomplete="off"` is deliberately ignored by all major browsers on password fields (Chromium and Mozilla policy, dating to 2014/v30) so that user password managers continue to work. If the user accepts the save prompt, the bot token is written to the browser's credential vault, keyed to the project-settings URL, and synced across devices via Google Password Manager / iCloud Keychain. AC17 requires the token never to leave the frontend; the password vault is a browser feature outside the application's control, so this is arguably out of scope, but it is a new residual exposure that did not exist with `type="text"` (text inputs honour `autocomplete="off"`).
findings.impact: Long-lived bearer token may be persisted in the user's browser password manager and synced across their signed-in devices. Risk is amplified if (a) the user shares the device, (b) the device is later compromised, or (c) the user later forgets the field was a token rather than a password and treats the vault entry as low-sensitivity.
findings.recommendation: Add `autocomplete="new-password"` to the bot-token input. Chrome and Edge treat this as a directive not to offer the save prompt; Firefox as a hint not to autofill from prior saved entries. Masking semantics of `type="password"` are preserved, so the round-1 shoulder-surf fix is unaffected. Example: `<input id="bot-token" v-model="tokenInput" type="password" autocomplete="new-password" spellcheck="false" ...>`. Optional belt-and-braces: also add `data-1p-ignore` (1Password) and `data-lpignore="true"` (LastPass) for third-party managers. Not blocking; do not regress on this round.

non_findings_explicitly_checked: Watcher vs onConfirmDisconnect race — both writes set the same boolean to false; Vue ref equality short-circuits the second write. No double-mutation.
Watcher vs onConfirmDisconnect error path — disconnect() throws BEFORE current is cleared, so the watcher does not fire; the catch block closes the modal explicitly. State consistent.

Watcher vs closeDisconnectModal — closeDisconnectModal early-returns when disconnecting === true; the watcher intentionally does not honour that guard, but the only path that mutates current to null during disconnecting === true is the success path of disconnect itself, where the early close is the desired UX.

Watcher firing on initial mount — botStore.current starts as null, and Vue's watch() does NOT fire on the initial value unless { immediate: true } is set. The code does not pass that option. No spurious modal close on first render.

Watcher firing during a stale-current 404 — fetch() (bot.ts:24-29) sets current.value = null on 404; the modal cannot be open at that point because the Connect form is what's rendered when current is null. No regression.
Watcher leaking memory after page unmount — `watch()` inside `<script setup>` auto-disposes on component unmount via the current Vue instance's scope. No leak.
type="password" + spellcheck="false" — spellcheck retained, prevents inline browser dictionary from receiving the token. Correct.

Token in input element's `defaultValue` / DOM serialization — input has no `value=` attribute and v-model binds the IDL property, not the attribute; outerHTML never contains the token. Verified by the existing bot.spec.ts:366 token-regex assertion against the full DOM.

Vue Devtools exposure of `tokenInput` ref — Pinia/Vue devtools record reactive state; production Vue disables devtools. The new `finally`-block clear shortens the window during which the ref holds the token to a single microtask after the network call resolves.
AC17/AC18/AC19/AC23 — round-1 audit confirmed all four pass; round-2 changes do not regress any of them. The new watcher tightens AC19 by sealing the empty-`@` render path.
Hardcoded secrets — no embedded API keys, tokens, passwords, or connection strings in bot.vue, bot.ts, or any audited file. Fixture token in bot.spec.ts is test-only and labelled 'Fake'.
CSRF / Authz / XSS / SSRF / Insecure deserialization — unchanged from round-1; round-2 surface (template watcher + input type attribute + finally-block reorder) does not introduce new vectors.
